messages.text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?
2. I’d like the coffee setup working again, but I can’t take on coordinating the repair myself.
Mostly, I’d like something simpler that doesn’t need much upkeep. I’m pretty worn out by the end of the day, so I couldn’t take on repairs or a cleaning rota.

2. I want it repaired and kept because it was my late father’s. Keeping it going matters to me, even though the constant breakdowns are wearing me down. Any repair discussion needs to fit into short slots.
I don’t know who owns the machine or who would pay for repairs. The grinder seems to be working; I haven’t noticed a problem with it.

I do understand why B wants to keep it. Short slots alone wouldn’t make me comfortable taking on repairs or follow-up, so I’d still lean toward a simpler machine with little upkeep and no ongoing duties assigned to me.

5. B: I can manage a 10–15 minute discussion, not a long meeting or coordinating the repair. A repair technician should inspect it. I’d still favor trying a repair without a guarantee it’ll stop breaking; if it keeps failing, we should reconsider.
I don’t know who holds the office budget. I lean toward option one, if the budget holder approves it and no follow-up duties fall to me.
I’d be willing to try option one if the repair and follow-up are handled by someone else, with a review date agreed in advance. I’d still prefer a simpler machine if the repair doesn’t hold.
Yes, I agree with option one if the budget holder approves. I don’t know who owns it or controls the budget; the office manager or whoever handles purchasing may know.
No, I’m not able to take that on. Please ask A or B.
I’m afraid I’d rather not take on even the asking; perhaps B can check with the office manager or purchasing, as suggested.
Yes. I can send a short message asking who owns it and who approves the repair cost.
I haven’t sent the message yet. I’ll ask the office manager or purchasing who owns it and who approves the cost; we haven’t agreed a review date yet.
